drug_class: Calcium Channel Blocker + ACE Inhibitor Combination
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two different medicines that work together to help lower your blood pressure more effectively than either one alone. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain.
how_it_works: Amlodipine works by relaxing and widening your blood vessels, kind of like loosening a tight garden hose so water flows through more easily. Benazepril blocks a chemical in your body called angiotensin, which normally causes your blood vessels to tighten up. Together, these two medicines help your heart pump blood with less effort and keep your blood pressure at a healthier level.
common_side_effects: Some people notice swelling in the ankles or feet, a dry cough, dizziness especially when standing up quickly, flushing or feeling warm, and headache. These are usually mild and may improve over time. Let your doctor or pharmacist know if any of these bother you.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless your doctor says it is okay, since benazepril can raise potassium levels. Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease, liver disease, or are allergic to ACE inhibitors. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you notice swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, as this can be a rare but serious reaction called angioedema.
typical_dosing: This medicine is usually taken once a day, with or without food. The most common starting dose is one capsule containing amlodipine 2.5 mg and benazepril 10 mg per day. Your doctor may adjust your dose depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. Try to take it at the same time each day and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
